This lesson introduces the capacitor. The capacitor is a simple yet extremely important electronic device.
INTRODUCTIONM
You will learn that capacitors have different shapes and values.
Operation and characteristics of the capacitor are described in both AC and DC circuits.
Let's begin the lesson on INTRODUCTION TO CAPACITORS......................
LESSON MENU
The capacitor is a component that has the ability to store an electrical charge.
DISCUSSION
In this circuit the capacitor is able to store an electrical charge equal to the applied voltage.
The capacitor is constructed from two plates separated by a non-conducting dielectric.
The capacitor is constructed from two plates separated by a non-conducting dielectric..
DEFINITION

DIELECTRIC - Dielectric is an insulating material used to separate the plates of a capacitor. This material cannot conduct but it can store an electric charge. Some materials used for a dielectric are glass, ceramics, mica, paper, teflon, oil, and air.
With the switch closed, current flows until the capacitor reaches a charge equal to the source voltage. Let's look at this process step-by-step.
Electrons flow from the negative terminal of the battery to the negative plate of the capacitor.
Charge flows from the positive terminal of the battery to the positive plate of the capacitor.r.
The positive terminal of the battery attracts electrons from the positive plate of the capacitor.
The negative terminal of the battery attracts the charge from the positive plate of the capacitor..
Electrons DO NOT travel through the capacitor. The dielectric is an insulator that blocks electrons.
Charge DOES NOT travel through the capacitor. The dielectric is an insulator that blocks the charge.
The charge builds up on the plate nearest the positive terminal and is repelled from the plate nearest the negative termianl.
Electrons build up on the plate nearest the negative terminal and are repelled from the plate nearest the positive terminal.

The effect is one plate has a positive charge and the other plate has a negative charge.
An electrostatic field exists between the plates of the capacitor allowing the dielectric to store a charge.

NON-LINEAR - The graph on the left shows a linear charge. Linear charges are constant. The rate of charge is constant from 0 to 10 volts.
DEFINITION
The graph on the right shows a non-linear charge. Non-linear charges are not constant. The rate of charge varies from 0 to 10 volts.
Notice that the non-linear voltage increases at a faster rate between 0 and 8 volts than from 8 to 10 volts. At 8 volts the charging rate slows down.........................
Charging is rapid initially and then slows as the capacitor reaches a voltage equal to the applied voltage.
Current flow is initially high and as charging slows, current flow also slows, eventually reaching zero.
The charged capacitor discharges through leakage or by applying a discharge circuit.

LEAKAGE - A capacitor is designed to hold a charge indefinitely. However, the dielectric material is NOT a perfect insulator. Some electrons flow across to the opposite plate. This electron flow is called Leakage.

LEAKAGE - A capacitor is designed to hold a charge indefinitely. However, the dielectric material is NOT a perfect insulator. Some charge will flow across to the opposite plate. This flow is called Leakage.
DEFINITION
The charged capacitor discharges through leakage or by applying a discharge circuit...
To discharge the capacitor manually, a circuit path must exist between the two plates.
The amount of time a capacitor holds a charge is determined by the quality of the dielectric.
If an AC voltage is applied to a capacitor, the capacitor must change polarity as the applied voltage changes.
The polarity of the capacitor changes at the same frequency as the applied voltage.
There are three classifications of capacitors:.............
Non-polarized capacitors are general purpose capacitors used to isolate one circuit from another, block unwanted signals, and produce wave shapes.
The schematic symbol for a non-polarized capacitor shows no difference between the positive and negative plate.
The electrolytic capacitor is polarity sensitive. A major use for this capacitor is filtering power supplies.
The schematic symbol for an electrolytic capacitor shows a difference between the positive and negative plates.
The variable capacitor provides varying amounts of capacitance. Transmitters and receivers use variable capacitors..
The schematic symbol for a variable capacitor contains an arrow indicating an adjustment.

DISCUSSION
The capacitor is labeled to indicate the amount of capacitance and the working voltage.
The Farad is the basic unit of capacitance. One farad is very large. Microfarad or Picofarad are more common units of capacitance.

DEFINITION
WORKING VOLTAGE - Working voltage is the maximum voltage that can be steadily applied to the capacitor without the capacitor breaking down (shorting).

The amount of capacitance is determined by the combined factors of plate size, distance between plates, and the dielectric material.
Plate size is a factor in the value of capacitance. The larger the plate area, the more capacitance.
The distance between plates is also a factor. The closer the plates are, the more capacitance.
The dielectric material also determines capacitance. All dielectric materials are given values. Oil
